# Interchange

19 tools. Back to the [index](README.md).

## `can_reset_interchange_actor`

*Read-only.*

Report, read-only, whether Interchange can reset an actor of the editor world (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::CanResetActor, which needs a bound UInterchangeSceneImportAsset); returns actor_path and can_reset. The actor is found by full object path or by object name in the persistent level, not by label.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_path` | string | yes | Full object path of the actor (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap.MyMap:PersistentLevel.ActorName_0") or its object name in the persistent level of the editor world (e.g. "StaticMeshActor_3"); labels are not matched. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_path: string, can_reset: bool }`

## `can_reset_interchange_world`

*Read-only.*

Report, read-only, whether Interchange can reset a world (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::CanResetWorld): the map asset world_path names, loaded if needed, or the current editor world. Returns can_reset, is_editor_world and resolved_world_path. Run the reset with reset_interchange_level_asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `world_path` | string | no | World asset path (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap") or fully-qualified object path. Empty = current editor world. |

**Returns:** `{ world_path: string, can_reset: bool, is_editor_world: bool }`

## `can_translate_interchange_source_data`

*Read-only.*

Whether a registered Interchange translator can read a source file (a path on disk or an asset path). Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file_path` | string | yes | Path of the source file to test on disk (e.g. "C:/Assets/Mesh.fbx"), or an Unreal asset path. Passed to UInterchangeManager::CreateSourceData. |
| `scene_only` | boolean | no | When true, restrict the check to scene translators (bSceneOnly). Defaults to false (any translator type). |

**Returns:** `{ file_path: string, scene_only: bool, can_translate: bool }`

## `create_interchange_pipeline_asset`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create an Interchange pipeline asset of a concrete pipeline class (the generic texture, mesh, material, animation, audio, scenes, groom or assets pipelines, glTF, sparse volume texture, MaterialX). Idempotent: an object of that name already in package_path is returned with already_existed:true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pipeline_class_path` | string | yes | Class path of the concrete (non-abstract) UInterchangePipelineBase subclass to instantiate (e.g. "/Script/InterchangePipelines.InterchangeGenericAssetsPipeline"), loaded via LoadClass. |
| `asset_name` | string | yes | Name of the new pipeline asset (the object/package name under package_path). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Destination UE content folder for the new pipeline asset (e.g. "/Game/Pipelines"). Defaults to "/Game". |

**Returns:** `{ pipeline_path: string, class: string, already_existed: bool, note: string }`

## `get_interchange_asset_import_data`

*Read-only.*

Read the Interchange import data (UInterchangeAssetImportData) of an asset loaded by package or object path: its source_filenames, display_labels, the pipeline objects stored on it (class, name, object path of each) and whether it holds a node container; with include_node_container, also that container's root_uids and every factory node (uid, display_label and the class of the object that factory produces) -- what an Interchange import produced. An asset imported through the legacy factory path, or never imported, has none: that answers present=false with zeros and empty lists, a normal state and not an error; only a path that does not load is an error. Read-only: it writes nothing and needs no PIE. The legacy UAssetImportData of a factory import (source file and timestamp): get_asset_import_data; replace the pipeline stack: set_interchange_pipelines; reimport from this data: reimport_interchange_asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path (e.g. "/Game/Foo/Foo") or fully-qualified object path ("/Game/Foo/Foo.Foo") |
| `include_node_container` | boolean | no | Optional bool, default false: add root_uids, factory_node_count and factory_nodes from the import data's node container (empty when there is none) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, present: bool, pipelines_count: number, pipelines: [{ class: string, name: string, path: string }], has_node_container: bool, source_filenames: [string], display_labels: [string], root_uids?: [string], factory_node_count?: number, factory_nodes?: [{ uid: string, class: string, display_label: string }] }`

## `get_interchange_pipeline_properties`

*Read-only.*

Read the editable (EditAnywhere) properties of an Interchange pipeline asset by reflection, inherited ones included: each entry gives name, C++ type and, unless class_only is true, the current value as JSON (left out when it cannot be converted). The values are the in-memory ones, so edits made with set_interchange_pipeline_properties and not yet saved already show. Read-only: it writes nothing and needs no PIE. A path that does not load as a UInterchangePipelineBase is an error. Discover the names with class_only=true, write them with set_interchange_pipeline_properties and persist with save_interchange_pipeline; the pipelines an imported asset used: get_interchange_asset_import_data; a new pipeline asset: create_interchange_pipeline_asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pipeline_path` | string | yes | Object path of the pipeline asset to read (loaded via LoadObject, must be a UInterchangePipelineBase), e.g. "/Game/Pipelines/MyMeshPipeline.MyMeshPipeline". |
| `class_only` | boolean | no | When true, return only the EditAnywhere property NAMES and types (no values) for discovery. Defaults to false (includes current values). |

**Returns:** `{ pipeline_path: string, class: string, properties: [{ name: string, type: string, value?: any }], property_count: number }`

## `get_interchange_project_settings`

*Read-only.*

Read the project's Interchange settings, the live class defaults of UInterchangeProjectSettings as Project Settings shows them. For content import: the default pipeline stack, every pipeline stack with its pipeline paths, the per-asset-type default-stack overrides, the import dialog class and the import and reimport dialog flags. For scene import: the default stack, the two dialog flags and only a count of its per-translator dialog overrides. Plus the file picker, generic pipeline and converter default pipeline classes, the static mesh smoothing fallback flag and the Interchange groups. Read-only, with no parameters. Change the default stack with set_interchange_pipeline_stack_default; read one pipeline asset with get_interchange_pipeline_properties; the formats translators accept: get_interchange_supported_formats.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ content_import_settings: { default_pipeline_stack: string, import_dialog_class: string, b_show_import_dialog: bool, b_show_reimport_dialog: bool, pipeline_stacks: [{ name: string, pipelines: [string] }], pipeline_stacks_count: int, default_pipeline_stack_override: [{ translator_type: string, stack_name: string }] }, scene_import_settings: { default_pipeline_stack: string, b_show_import_dialog: bool, b_show_reimport_dialog: bool, per_translator_dialog_override_count: int }, file_picker_class: string, generic_pipeline_class: string, converter_default_pipeline: string, b_static_mesh_use_smooth_edges_if_smoothing_information_is_missing: bool, interchange_groups: [{ display_name: string, unique_id: string, default_pipeline_stack: string, b_show_import_dialog: bool, b_show_reimport_dialog: bool }], interchange_groups_count: int }`

## `get_interchange_supported_formats`

*Read-only.*

Report Interchange framework availability and list the file extensions supported by registered Interchange translators of a given type.  Calls UInterchangeManager::GetSupportedFormats(EInterchangeTranslatorType) (InterchangeManager.h, INTERCHANGEENGINE_API) and IsInterchangeImportEnabled(). The 5.8 enum has Invalid / Assets / Actors / Scenes (Scenes = Assets|Actors). Accepts aliases "Assets", "Actors", "Scenes", and "AssetsAndScene" (mapped to Scenes). The registered translator set is private in 5.8, so availability is reported as enabled (= import enabled AND at least one supported asset format) with the per-type format counts.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `translator_type` | string | no | Translator type: "Assets" [default], "Actors", "Scenes", or the spec alias "AssetsAndScene" |

**Returns:** `{ translator_type: string, format_count: number, formats: [string], enabled: bool, import_enabled: bool, asset_format_count: number, actor_format_count: number, scene_format_count: number }`

## `import_interchange_asset`

*Destructive.*

Import a source file synchronously through the Interchange manager: unattended, no dialogs, replacing existing assets unless replace_existing is false. When the InterchangeImport plugin is not loaded the note says so.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file_path` | string | yes | Path of the source file to import on disk (e.g. "C:/Assets/Mesh.fbx"). Passed to UInterchangeManager::CreateSourceData. |
| `destination_path` | string | no | Destination UE content folder for the imported asset(s) (e.g. "/Game/Meshes"). Defaults to "/Game/Imported". |
| `replace_existing` | boolean | no | When true, overwrite an existing asset at the destination (bReplaceExisting). Defaults to true. |

**Returns:** `{ file_path: string, destination_path: string, imported: bool, count: number, imported_objects: [string], note: string }`

## `register_interchange_factory`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Register a factory class -- the Interchange step that creates one kind of asset, such as a texture or a static mesh, from translated data -- with the Interchange manager for this editor session. Nothing is written to disk and the registration ends when the editor closes; the engine registers its own factories on startup, so this is for a class whose plugin did not. The manager keeps one factory per asset class and the first one registered stays: when another factory already makes that asset class the call is refused and names it. Registering the factory that is already active changes nothing and reports already_registered=true, so a repeat call is harmless (idempotent). A class that does not load, is abstract or is not a UInterchangeFactoryBase subclass is refused. The reader of a source file format registers with register_interchange_translator.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `factory_class_path` | string | yes | Class path of the factory class, e.g. "/Script/InterchangeImport.InterchangeTextureFactory"; loaded with LoadClass. |

**Returns:** `{ factory_class_path, class, asset_class, registered, already_registered }`

## `register_interchange_translator`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Register a translator class -- the Interchange reader of one or more source file formats -- with the Interchange manager for this editor session, so imports and get_interchange_supported_formats pick up its formats. Nothing is written to disk and the registration ends when the editor closes; the engine registers its own translators on startup, so this is for a class whose plugin did not. The class must load and be a concrete UInterchangeTranslatorBase subclass: anything else is refused before it is registered, since the manager would assert on the next format query. A class already registered changes nothing and reports already_registered=true, so a repeat call is harmless (idempotent). A factory, which turns translated data into assets, registers with register_interchange_factory; whether a given file can be read: can_translate_interchange_source_data.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `translator_class_path` | string | yes | Class path of the translator class, e.g. "/Script/InterchangeImport.InterchangeImageWrapperTranslator"; loaded with LoadClass. |

**Returns:** `{ translator_class_path, class, registered, already_registered?, supported_formats: [string] }`

|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path (e.g. "/Game/Foo/Foo") or fully-qualified object path ("/Game/Foo/Foo.Foo") |

## `reset_interchange_actors`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Run an Interchange reset (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::ResetActors) on the editor-world actors listed by object path or persistent-level object name; the library skips actors that fail CanResetActor, and the reply does not say which were reset. Returns count, resolved and unresolved_paths. Check first with can_reset_interchange_actor.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_paths` | array | yes | Actors to reset, each a full object path (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap.MyMap:PersistentLevel.ActorName_0") or an object name in the persistent level; labels are not matched, and empty or unknown entries land in unresolved_paths. |

**Returns:** `{ count: number, resolved: number, unresolved_paths: [string], note: string }`

## `reset_interchange_level_asset`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Run an Interchange reset on a level (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::ResetLevelAsset), the map world_path names or the current editor world, only when the Interchange.FeatureFlags.InterchangeReset CVar is on and CanResetWorld is true; otherwise it does nothing and the call fails (reset false, with the reason in note). It does not save. Returns reset, can_reset, cvar_enabled and a note.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `world_path` | string | no | World asset path (e.g. "/Game/Maps/MyMap") or fully-qualified object path. Empty = current editor world. |

**Returns:** `{ world_path: string, resolved_world_path: string, reset: bool, can_reset: bool, cvar_enabled: bool, note: string }`

## `reset_interchange_scene_import_asset`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Call the Interchange reset of a UInterchangeSceneImportAsset (UInterchangeEditorScriptLibrary::ResetSceneImportAsset); other asset classes are refused. The engine only resets while the Interchange.FeatureFlags.InterchangeReset CVar is 1: with it at 0 the call does nothing and fails (reset false). The reset itself returns nothing, so reset true means it ran, not what it changed. Use reset_interchange_level_asset for a level.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UInterchangeSceneImportAsset (e.g. "/Game/Imports/MyScene.MyScene") |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, reset: bool, cvar_enabled: bool, note: string }`

## `save_interchange_pipeline`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write the package of an Interchange pipeline asset (a UInterchangePipelineBase loaded by object path) over its .uasset on disk, dirty or not, through the shared asset save; saved false makes success false and save_error carries the measured cause. It is the persist step after create_interchange_pipeline_asset and set_interchange_pipeline_properties, which change memory only; repeating it is idempotent. Like save_asset it refuses during PIE and under a read-only root. A path that does not load as a pipeline is an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pipeline_path` | string | yes | Object path of the pipeline asset whose package is written to disk (loaded via LoadObject, must be a UInterchangePipelineBase). |

**Returns:** `{ pipeline_path: string, file_path: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_interchange_pipeline_properties`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write settings of an Interchange pipeline asset -- what a pipeline does at import, such as whether it imports materials or how it names the assets -- by reflection, from a {name: value} object in which a value is a scalar, an object for a struct or an array for a TArray. Each value overwrites the one in memory, records no undo step and is not saved: save_interchange_pipeline writes the asset to disk. Names are applied one by one; one that does not exist, is not editable in the editor or does not convert is skipped and listed with the reason in skipped, and the others are still written. An empty properties object is refused. Writing the same values again leaves the asset as it was (idempotent). The names, types and current values come from get_interchange_pipeline_properties; to choose which pipelines an imported asset uses, set_interchange_pipelines.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pipeline_path` | string | yes | Object path of the pipeline asset, e.g. "/Game/Pipelines/MyMeshPipeline.MyMeshPipeline"; it must load as a UInterchangePipelineBase. |
| `properties` | object | yes | {property_name: value}, with names as get_interchange_pipeline_properties lists them; a struct takes an object of its fields and a TArray an array. |

**Returns:** `{ pipeline_path, applied_count, skipped_count, skipped?: [string], note }`

## `set_interchange_pipeline_stack_default`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Choose the named pipeline stack Interchange uses by default for content imports (assets) or scene imports (levels) -- the DefaultPipelineStack that Project Settings > Interchange shows -- and write it to the project's DefaultEngine.ini, so it outlives the editor session. The stack must already exist in that import path's pipeline stacks: an unknown name is refused with the list of the ones there, and so is a read-only DefaultEngine.ini, both before anything changes. The previous default is overwritten and returned in previous_stack_name; choosing the stack that is already the default changes nothing (changed=false), so a repeat call is harmless (idempotent). No undo step is recorded. The content stacks and both current defaults are listed by get_interchange_project_settings; to choose the pipelines of one imported asset instead, use set_interchange_pipelines.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content_or_scene` | string | yes | Which default to set: "content" for asset imports (ContentImportSettings) or "scene" for level imports (SceneImportSettings). Case-insensitive. |
| `stack_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing pipeline stack of that import path, e.g. "Assets"; matched without case. |

**Returns:** `{ content_or_scene, stack_name, previous_stack_name, changed, config_file, applied }`

## `set_interchange_pipelines`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Replace the UInterchangePipelineBase stack on an asset's UInterchangeAssetImportData.  Loads the asset + its UInterchangeAssetImportData, resolves each path in ``pipeline_paths`` via LoadObject&lt;UObject>, then calls ID->SetPipelines(InPipelines) (InterchangeAssetImportData.h, INTERCHANGEENGINE_API). Idempotent: SetPipelines resets TransientPipelines before applying (impl InterchangeAssetImportData.cpp). Marks the package dirty so the change persists on save.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path (e.g. "/Game/Foo/Foo") |
| `pipeline_paths` | array | yes | Array of fully-qualified pipeline asset paths (UObject* resolved via LoadObject). Entries that fail to resolve are reported in ``unresolved_paths`` but do not abort the call. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, present: bool, pipeline_count: number, unresolved_paths: [string] }`
